newsitem.title: MEXICO: ING Barings raises estimate for Mexico GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings raises estimate for Mexico GDP growth.

text.p: ING Barings has revised its forecast of 1996 Mexican economic growth to 4.3 percent from a previous estimate of 3.4 percent, the investment bank said Monday in a news release.
At the same time, ING Barings raised its forecast of 1997 gross domestic product growth to 4.0 percent from 3.6 percent.
Sergio Martin, the firm's Mexico economist, reported the new estimates in the latest Emerging Markets Weekly Report, ING Barings said.
The more optimistic forecast is supported by positive trends in Mexico's industrial production, exports, imports and employment, ING Barings said.

Many economists have upgraded estimates for 1996 Mexican GDP growth to more than four percent after the government's announcement last week that second-quarter GDP grew by 7.2 percent compared with the same period last year. The increase was higher than generally expected.
